'''Kevin Burleson''' (born September 4, 1979) is an  American professional [[basketball]] coach, and a former professional basketball player. He is currently an assistant coach for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Minnesota]] [[Minnesota Golden Gophers|Golden Gophers]] and began his professional career in the [[Germany|German]] basketball league. He played for the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in 2005–06. During a 34-game stretch, Burleson played in 20 of those games and, during that period, missed 35 field-goal attempts in a row.

==Early life==
Burleson was born in [[Seattle, Washington]]. He was born to a prolific sporting family: his father, [[Al Burleson]], played [[defensive back]] in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) and the [[United States Football League]] (USFL). His older brother Alvin Jr. played [[college football]] for the [[University of Washington]] [[Washington Huskies|Huskies]] and the [[Western Illinois University]] [[Western Illinois Leathernecks|Leathernecks]]. His younger brother [[Nate Burleson|Nate]] was a wide receiver in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), while younger brother Lyndale played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Nevada, Reno|University of Nevada]] [[Nevada Wolf Pack|Wolf Pack]].<ref name=Burleson>{{cite news |title= Burlesons are the first family of Seattle sports|first= Dan|last= Raley|newspaper= Seattle Post-Intelligencer|date= September 13, 2006|url= http://www.seattlepi.com/football/284893_family13.html|access-date= October 19, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2148107 |title=Sonics sign Moore weeks after losing James |newspaper=[[ESPN]] |date=August 31, 2005 |access-date=October 19, 2010}}</ref> Kevin and Nate Burleson are one of only two sets of siblings in which one played in the NBA and one in the NFL.<ref name=Canada>{{cite news|title= Lions' Burleson proud of Canadian roots|first= Bob|last= Duff|newspaper= [[Montreal Gazette]]|date= October 18, 2010|url= https://montrealgazette.com/sports/Lions+Burleson+proud+Canadian+roots/3690320/story.html|access-date= October 19, 2010|archive-date= April 21, 2023|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230421214629/https://montrealgazette.com/sports/Lions+Burleson+proud+Canadian+roots/3690320/story.html|url-status= dead}}</ref> Like his brothers he played several sports early on, but gave up baseball as he found it too slow, and gave up football for fear of an injury that would prevent him from playing basketball.<ref name=Burleson/>

Burleson graduated from [[O'Dea High School]] after transferring from [[Garfield High School (Seattle, Washington)|Garfield High School]] after his freshman year.<ref name=Burleson /> At O'Dea, Burleson earned three letters in basketball and one in track and field and played basketball under coach [[Phil Lumpkin]]. In his junior year, Burleson helped O'Dea go undefeated through a 29-game season and win the state title.<ref name="Minn bio">{{cite web|title=Kevin Burleson|url=http://www.gophersports.com/Sports/player.asp?player_id=794&sport_id=mbasket|publisher=Minnesota Golden Gophers|access-date=February 25, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031102031340/http://www.gophersports.com/Sports/player.asp?player_id=794&sport_id=mbasket|archive-date=November 2, 2003}}</ref>

==College career==
Burleson was offered a basketball scholarship to the [[University of Washington]], but opted instead to attend the [[University of Minnesota]] for a chance to play in the [[Big Ten Conference]].<ref name=Burleson/> He played for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball]] team from 1999 to 2003 after redshirting the 1998–99 season. Minnesota made the [[2001 National Invitation Tournament]] (NIT), and Burleson scored a season-high 21 points in Minnesota's win over [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] in the first round. As a junior, Burleson led Minnesota with 146 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and had an assist/turnover ratio 146–58.<ref name="Minn bio"/>

==Professional career==
Burleson began his professional career in Germany. He played for the [[USC Heidelberg]] in the 2003–2004 season and for the [[Walter Tigers Tübingen]] of [[Basketball Bundesliga]] in the 2004–2005 season. He was then signed by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] of the NBA on August 31, 2005. He played with the Bobcats for the 2005–2006 season, but was subsequently cut.

In the 2006 [[NBA Development League]] draft, the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] picked Burleson as the fourth overall pick in the first round.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_2006.html 2006 D-League draft results] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070219055015/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_2006.html |date=2007-02-19 }}</ref> Burleson played for the Flyers for the {{nbay|2006}} season, then signed with the [[Turkish Basketball League]] team [[Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi|Mersin Büyükşehir Belediye]] for the 2007–2008 season.<ref name="kboi2">{{cite news|url=http://www.kboi2.com/sports/38650357.html |title=Stampede sign former NBA player Kevin Burleson |newspaper=[[KBOI-TV]] |date=January 29, 2009 |access-date=July 21, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718232042/http://www.kboi2.com/sports/38650357.html |archive-date=July 18, 2011 }}</ref> In January 2009 he signed with the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]] the day after being traded from the [[Iowa Energy]].<ref name="kboi2"/><ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_08-09.html Transactions, D-League, 2008–09] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151219004752/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_08-09.html |date=2015-12-19 }}</ref> Burleson finished his career with the Egyptian team [[Al-Ittihad Alexandria]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.teamID_92444.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2010.roundID_7065.playerID_46600.html|title = Kevin Burleson | EuroChallenge (2010) | FIBA Europe}}</ref>
==Coaching career==

He began his coaching career with the Houston Rockets. He mainly focused on player development. 

On June 15, 2018, Burleson was hired as assistant coach/player development coach for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web |date=June 15, 2018 |title=Memphis Grizzlies announce assistant coaching staff |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-announce-assistant-coaching-staff-180615 |access-date=June 15, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> 

On June 27, 2019, Burleson was hired by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] as a player development coach.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 27, 2019 |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Add to Coaching Staff |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-add-coaching-staff |access-date=June 27, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> 

After three seasons in Minnesota, where he was head coach of the team in the NBA Summer League, in September 2022, he took over as head coach of the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the G League.<ref>[https://rocketswire-eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rockets/2022/09/07/rio-grande-valley-vipers-name-kevin-burleson-as-new-head-coach/77510170007/ Rio Grande Valley Vipers name Kevin Burleson as new head coach] usatoday.com, 7-sep-2022</ref>

On July 12, 2024, Burleson was hired as assistant coach for the [[Detroit Pistons]]. <ref>{{Cite web|last=Sankofa II|first=Omari|date=July 12, 2024|title=Detroit Pistons hire Luke Walton, Kevin Burleson as assistant coaches|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2024/07/12/detroit-pistons-hire-luke-walton-kevin-burleson-assistant-coaches/74390217007/|access-date=July 12, 2024|website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref>
